items.name: Intro
items.description: Opening passage before the first vocal. Sets key, tempo, mood and often previews a riff or melody that returns later.

items.name: Verse
items.description: Section that repeats its music with new lyrics each time. Carries the story, detail and scene-setting that the chorus then sums up.

items.name: Pre-chorus
items.description: Short link between verse and chorus that builds tension, often by rising melody or changed harmony, so the chorus lands as a release.

items.name: Chorus
items.description: Main refrain: the same music and (mostly) the same words every time. The emotional centre and the part listeners sing back; usually carries the title.

items.name: Post-chorus
items.description: Short extra section right after a chorus that keeps its energy going, often a chant, riff or repeated tag line.

items.name: Bridge
items.description: Contrasting section, usually once, placed late. Changes melody, chords or lyric angle to break repetition before a final return to the chorus.

items.name: Hook
items.description: Short, catchy musical or lyrical idea built to stick in memory. It can be a riff, a phrase or a title line, and may live inside any section.

items.name: Interlude
items.description: Brief instrumental or spoken passage between sections that gives a breather or a change of scene.

items.name: Instrumental break
items.description: Section where an instrument takes the lead in place of the vocal, such as a solo, usually over verse or chorus chords.

items.name: Breakdown
items.description: Stripped-back section where most layers drop out, often before a build-up and final chorus or drop.

items.name: Outro
items.description: Closing passage that winds the song down, by fading, repeating a motif, or a clean ending. Also called coda.

items.name: Verse-chorus
items.description: Most common pop and rock form: verses tell the story, repeated choruses carry the main message, one bridge adds contrast.

items.name: Verse-pre-chorus-chorus
items.description: Verse-chorus form with a pre-chorus ramp into every chorus for a stronger lift.

items.name: AABA (32-bar)
items.description: Classic Tin Pan Alley and jazz standard form: two matching 8-bar A sections, a contrasting 8-bar bridge, then A again. The title usually sits in the A sections.

items.name: Strophic
items.description: Every verse reuses the same music with new words, with no chorus. Typical of folk songs, ballads and hymns.

items.name: 12-bar blues
items.description: Blues form built on one 12-bar chord cycle repeated for each verse. Lyrics often state a line, repeat it, then answer it.

items.name: Verse with refrain
items.description: Verses that each end on a repeated title line (a refrain) instead of a separate chorus section.

items.name: Through-composed
items.description: Music keeps changing with the text and does not repeat sections. Fits narrative or dramatic songs.

items.name: Modern pop (hook-first)
items.description: Streaming-era shape: a hook or chorus teaser up front, short intro, pre-chorus lifts and a post-chorus tag, compact length.
